summary.oneLiner: Dachepalli has transformed from a traditional textbook publisher into an integrated academic solutions platform, driven by in-house manufacturing of notebooks and uniforms, a scalable e-commerce platform (Pelican Edu Supply) tied to 150+ schools, and deep institutional partnerships — creating margin expansion, recurring revenue streams, and defensible market share growth in Tier 2/3 India.

hero.industry: Education / Academic Publishing & Integrated School Solutions

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Textbook: INR 70cr revenue (FY26), 10,000 schools across 15 states; Pelican E-commerce: INR 20cr revenue (FY26), 50 schools, 70% Dachepalli textbooks + 30% third-party + notebooks/stationery; Notebooks: in-house manufacturing launched (10 tons/day capacity); Uniforms: pilot in 3 schools, scaling to 50 existing Pelican schools in FY27; Stationery: not yet manufactured, white-label currently, target 30k units to trigger in-house production

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR 70cr+ from textbook business (FY27), INR 60cr+ from Pelican platform (textbooks, notebooks, stationery, uniforms) across 150 schools

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: INR 150cr+ (FY27), INR 220-230cr (FY28); margin: PAT 16-17% sustained, EBITDA to expand further with uniform scaling; order inflow: 100-150 new schools for Pelican platform; capex/commissioning: notebook capacity 10 tons/day (80% pre-booked), uniform stitching outsourced until 200-250 schools reached

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into 28 states + 8 UTs (from 15); stationery manufacturing (pens, geometry boxes) at 30k unit volume; curriculum licensing (e.g., The Money Tree); potential LMS platform monetization; international school exports (long-term)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 25.7% (FY26) driven by: 1) 40-50% paper cost decline since 2020 (INR 120/kg → INR 65/kg); 2) in-house printing (75% utilization); 3) notebook manufacturing replacing third-party purchases (higher margin); 4) uniform margins ~50% EBITDA (scaling to 50 schools in FY27); 5) Pelican platform reduces distribution cost

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Funds from IPO used to hire sales teams, enter 4 new states (UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam), and fund in-house capex (notebooks, printing); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; reinvestment prioritized over payout

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; management explicitly rejects traditional publishing model; emphasizes institutional stickiness, vertical integration, and platform scalability; acknowledges challenges (e.g., uniform logistics) but frames them as solvable with scale; targets INR 500cr+ revenue by FY29

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Regulatory scrutiny on school supply chain profit margins; 2) delayed school payments (200+ days debtor days due to academic cycle mismatch); 3) competition from Navneet/S. Chand entering e-commerce; 4) uniform supply chain complexity; 5) over-reliance on state board academic cycles

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 1) 200+ day debtor days are an accounting artifact — cash collection aligns with school reopening (June), not invoice date; 2) Pelican platform’s 50% textbook requirement is a stealth channel control mechanism — not just a sales channel but a school adoption tool; 3) ‘6 brands’ strategy is a market segmentation tactic to bypass school procurement rules that limit single-vendor adoption; 4) paper cost decline is structural — digital substitution in non-textbook paper use has permanently lowered input costs
